candidates.label: result

candidates.label: resultComment

Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: quest
candidates.comment: A quest relation between a game or video game series and a specific task or mission that players can complete for a reward. Also called mission, task, objective. Examples: "A role-playing game features a quest to 'defeat the dragon'.", "A video game series includes a quest to 'collect all artifacts'.", "An adventure game has a quest to 'rescue the princess'."

candidates.label: produces
candidates.comment: An outcome relation between a service and the tangible thing it generates or provides. Also called generates, yields, creates, provides. Examples: A government service produces a 'passport'. A licensing service produces a 'permit'. A printing service produces 'documents'.

candidates.label: resultReview
candidates.comment: The specific review created as the outcome of a review action. Also called generated review, review outcome, produced review. Examples: `ReviewAction on Product` resultReview `Customer's Product Review`, `ReviewAction on Movie` resultReview `Critic's Movie Review`, `ReviewAction on Service` resultReview `User Service Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: seeks

Examples: `Company X` seeks `Demand for Software Developers`, `Person Y` seeks `Demand for Used Car`, `Organization Z` seeks `Demand for Consulting Services`. Distinct from `offers`, which is about what is provided.

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: potentialAction

candidates.label: educationalCredentialAwarded

candidates.label: lesserOrEqual

candidates.label: highPrice

Examples: "An aggregate offer has a high price of $100.", "The offers have a high price of '99.99'.", "This collection of offers shows a high price."

candidates.label: nonEqual

An item list has itemListElement a ListItem for 'Task 1'. Distinct from item, which refers to the entity *within* a ListItem, not the ListItem itself or a direct string/entity in the list.

candidates.label: roleName

candidates.label: namedPosition
candidates.comment: A specific named position or role played by a person or organization within a larger organization. Also called role name, position title, job title. Examples: "Athlete Role namedPosition 'Quarterback'", "Employee Role namedPosition 'Senior Software Engineer'", "Board Member Role namedPosition 'Treasurer'". Distinct from roleName, which is a more general description of a role.

candidates.label: hasMolecularFunction
candidates.comment: A molecular function relation between a biochemical entity and its performed molecular function. Also called performs function, molecular role, functional activity. Examples: "A protein has a molecular function of enzyme activity.", "This BioChemEntity has a molecular function described by a defined term.", "The entity's molecular function is specified."

candidates.label: jobTitle
candidates.comment: An occupational role relation between a person and their formal designation within an organization. Also called position, role, occupation, professional title. Examples: A person has a jobTitle of 'Software Engineer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Chief Executive Officer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Marketing Manager'.

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: chemicalRole
candidates.comment: A functional relation describing the role played by a chemical substance or molecular entity within a chemical context. Also called "chemical function", "biochemical role", "molecular role". Examples: "Enzyme chemical role 'Catalyst'", "Drug chemical role 'Agonist'".

candidates.label: biologicalRole
candidates.comment: A defined term describing the role played by a biochemical entity within a biological context. Also called: biological function, physiological role, molecular role. Examples: "BioChemEntity 'Enzyme' biologicalRole 'Catalyst'", "BioChemEntity 'Hormone' biologicalRole 'Signaling Molecule'."

candidates.label: relevantOccupation
candidates.comment: A relevant occupation relation between a job posting and the specific occupation it describes. Also called job role, occupation type. Examples: "A job posting for 'Software Engineer' has a relevant occupation 'Software Developer'.", "A job posting for 'Nurse Practitioner' has a relevant occupation 'Registered Nurse'.", "A job posting for 'Marketing Manager' has a relevant occupation 'Marketing Professional'."

candidates.label: numberedPosition
candidates.comment: A number associated with an organization role, such as an athlete's jersey number. Also called role number, position number, identifier number. Examples: "Athlete Role numberedPosition 23", "Team Member Role numberedPosition 7", "Employee Role numberedPosition 101". Distinct from namedPosition, which is a textual name for a role.

candidates.label: position
candidates.comment: An ordinal attribute indicating the sequential position of an item within a series or list. Also called order, rank, sequence number, index. Examples: A list item has a position of '1'. A chapter in a book has a position of 'Chapter 3'. A search result has a position of '5'.

candidates.label: connectedTo
candidates.comment: A connection relation between an anatomical structure and other anatomical structures it is connected to. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "connects with". Examples: "Femur anatomical structure connectedTo Tibia", "Brain anatomical structure connectedTo Spinal cord".

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: follows
candidates.comment: A follows relation representing a generic uni-directional social connection between two people. Also called: is following, subscribes to, tracks. Examples: "Alice follows Bob", "Charlie follows David", "Eve follows Frank". Distinct from followee, which is the object of a follow action.

candidates.label: serviceAudience
candidates.comment: The specific group of people or entities for whom a service is intended or eligible. Also called target audience, service recipients, eligible users. Examples: `Healthcare Service` serviceAudience `Audience: Seniors`, `Educational Service` serviceAudience `Audience: Students`, `Financial Service` serviceAudience `Audience: Small Businesses`.

candidates.label: audience
candidates.comment: An intended group for whom a creative work, event, lodging business, play action, product, or service was created. Also called: target group, demographic, intended recipient. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Children's Book' audience 'Children'", "Event 'Tech Conference' audience 'Developers'", "Product 'Luxury Car' audience 'High-net-worth individuals'."

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

candidates.label: permitAudience
candidates.comment: A targeting relation between a permit and the specific audience it is intended for. Also called target group, eligible recipients, intended users. Examples: A fishing permit has a permit audience of 'Local Residents'. A building permit has a permit audience of 'Licensed Contractors'. A student permit has a permit audience of 'University Students'.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: actor
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) or event and a person or performing group who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actor is 'Tom Hanks'.", "A play's actor is 'The Ensemble Theatre'.", "An episode's actor is 'Jane Doe'." Distinct from actors, which is a deprecated property for the same concept.
